findings.claim: The probe accepts any binary printing `spar <anything>` with exit 0 and never compares against the pinned 0.40.0. A stale spar that does follow the --version convention passes, so the 'measuring with the wrong binary' trap the gate claims to close stays open.

Self-test 'ledger arithmetic' re-implements the filter on local literals rather than calling run()'s ledger code, so it cannot fail if run()'s newly/fixed/vanished logic regresses. The vanished-entry direction has no test at all.

findings.quoted_line: if cargo xtask check aadl-parse --module safety/aadl/semaphore.aadl; then
findings.claim: Negative control passes on any non-zero exit: REFUSED (3), usage (2) or a cargo build failure (101) all count as 'the gate rejects the model'. It should require exit 1 (Fail); xtask has distinct exit codes precisely for this.

The job that claims to measure with the PINNED spar bootstraps from an installer fetched from the mutable varve main branch and runs it with sh on a self-hosted runner, with no tag, commit pin, checksum or signature check.

Any non-zero spar exit (crash, unknown subcommand, missing file, I/O error) becomes 'PARSE FAILS', yet the summary says 'A PARSE FAILS row is always real'. A ledgered model that hits a spar error looks still-broken, and a mistyped --module path reads as 'rejected'.
